chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:
The Sunnah regarding the shaving (of the head) is that it should reach the bones.

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: The Sunnah; the recommended prophetic practice or tradition
key_terms.الْعَظْمَيْنِ: The two bones; referring to the depth of the shave reaching the bone

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended depth for shaving the head according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies the jurisprudential standard for ritual shaving, requiring the hair to be removed down to the level of the underlying bones, thereby ensuring a thorough and clean removal. It highlights the Shia emphasis on precision in acts of worship and personal grooming, linking physical cleanliness to spiritual purity. This ruling is often discussed in the context of *fitrah* (natural disposition) and the Prophet's tradition of maintaining hygiene.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup>, from Ali<sup>asws</sup> having said ‘
The Sunnah regarding the shaving (of the head) is that it should reach the bones’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: “Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has narrated from his ancestors, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, who have said, ‘
The sunnah about shaving is that it must reach the two bones (down to both temple bones).”’
